messages:
marco: Heads-up: seeing short ECC bursts on a handful of P4s in eu-west-1 over the last 3 days. dmesg shows short noisy ECC lines ~30s before Xid 13s. Can we add a lightweight preemptive snapshot harvester that keeps a rolling 60–120s dmesg/journal + nvidia-smi so we have context when we drain/replace?

dinesh: Yep. My proposal: agent-level in-memory ring buffer for kernel logs + a tiny journal tail + the last 2 nvidia-smi snapshots. Trigger persist+upload when ECC counter delta exceeds threshold in a window. Low disk churn, short TTL on upload.

carla: Agree on buffer. Few questions: retention/upload policy and how we avoid noisy floods (spurious uploads). Also how this ties into our existing log ingestion and ticketing.

marco: Minimal plan sketch: 1) ring buffer keeping last 120s of `dmesg -T` (kernel warnings/errors) + `journalctl -k --since "-2m"` stripped to kernel subsystem lines, plus `nvidia-smi -q -x` and a CSV snapshot. 2) trigger when ECC delta / 60s > configurable threshold (default 3). 3) on trigger, persist to `/var/tmp/gpu-harvest/<node>-<ts>.tgz` with a small manifest.json, then upload to short-lived S3 (24h TTL). 4) Post ticket to infra-tickets with link + attach to node metadata (tag). Debounce so we need 2 windows out of 3 before upload.

infra-bot: Note: systemd unit suggestion: `gpu-harvester.service` running as a privileged agent hook. Low CPU, runs in user namespaces. Sample config can be toggled per region.

ben: Can we avoid uploading whole `journalctl` by default? Prefer capturing `dmesg` + `journalctl -k --since` filtered to `NVRM|nvidia|kernel` and the device plugin unit. Keeps size down. Also prefer `.tgz` with a `manifest.json` instead of raw JSONL.

dinesh: Good call. We'll capture: `dmesg -T | tail -n 500`, `journalctl -k --since "-2m" -o short-iso | egrep -i "nvrm|nvidia|gpu|xid|ecc|nvlink"`, and `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,ecc.mode.current,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile --format=csv`. Persist both CSV and raw `nvidia-smi -q` XML.

marco: Also include kernel version, driver version, last-reset time, and node labels (rack, region, instance-type) in manifest so triage is faster.

carla: How to wire into ingestion? We should add a small parser that extracts Xid lines and ECC counters and index them into ES/ClickHouse for quick search. But only push parsed metadata; raw archive stays in S3.

ben: Quick one-liner for capture (for PR README):
```
mkdir -p /tmp/gpu-harvest && \
 dmesg -T | tail -n 500 > /tmp/gpu-harvest/dmesg.txt && \
 journalctl -k --since "-2m" | egrep -i "nvrm|nvidia|xid|ecc|nvlink" > /tmp/gpu-harvest/journal-k.txt && \
 nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,driver_version,ecc.errors.uncorrected.volatile,ecc.errors.corrected.volatile --format=csv > /tmp/gpu-harvest/gpu.csv && \
 nvidia-smi -q -x > /tmp/gpu-harvest/gpu.xml && \
 tar -czf /tmp/gpu-harvest-$(hostname)-$(date +%s).tgz -C /tmp gpu-harvest
```

dinesh: I'll add a tiny parser in the agent that emits JSON manifest keys: node, hostname, region, rack, gpu_index, driver, kernel, ecc_uncorrected_delta, ecc_corrected_delta, xid_events_found. Those go to our short-term index. Raw tar goes to S3.

carla: Add debounce: require 2 triggers in a 5-minute sliding window OR trigger immediately if Xid 13 observed. Many ECC blips are false positives.

oncall-rotations: I'll own canary deployment to 50 nodes in eu-west-1 next Monday morning. We should make region opt-in first. Also add a flag to suppress uploads during busy cycles to avoid hammering S3.

marco: Cost note: with 50-node canary and 24h TTL, upload volume should be trivial if debounce is tuned. Worst-case we can increase TTL/aggregation.

ben: Parser suggestion to extract Xid/ECC context (python snippet):
```python
# read dmesg lines and extract xid/ecc hits
import re, json
out=[]
for l in open('dmesg.txt'):
    if re.search(r'Xid|Ecc|UNC|Corrected|NVRM|GPU', l, re.I):
        out.append(l.strip())
print(json.dumps({'xid_lines': out}))
```

dinesh: I'll open the PR with the agent change, config flags: `ecc_threshold`, `ring_seconds`, `upload_bucket`, `ttl_hours`, `debounce_windows`. Will add unit tests for manifest shape.

carla: Runbook snippet for triage (to include in ticket): 1) open S3 tar, extract manifest, 2) check `gpu.csv` for ECC deltas and driver/kernel mismatch, 3) inspect dmesg for Xid patterns and nvlink errors, 4) correlate with allocation history and last workload PID. If ECC uncorrected > 0 or repeated Xid 13 -> schedule drain + replace.

oncall-rotations: Also flag: if multiple cards on same host have ECC errors, increase replacement priority (could be PMIC/hw-level).

infra-bot: CI note: PR must include integration test that simulates ECC counter bump and verifies upload and manifest fields. Will run on staging.

ben: small Q: filename convention? prefer `node-ts.tgz` with a `manifest.json` inside. keep filenames short.

marco: done. assign dinesh for PR. I'll draft the runbook and the alert updates. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
